gw_ops.check.inbound_down_no_part: the {title} protocol is down — not starting it: the gateway part is missing from the nftables table
gw_ops.check.no_compat_in: the iptables compatibility rule ({comment}) is missing: UFW cuts DNS and the path through xray
gw_ops.check.unit_down_no_part: {what} ({unit}) is down — not starting it: the gateway part is missing from the nftables table
gw_ops.check.unit_not_enabled: {what} ({unit}) isn’t enabled at boot — it won’t start after a reboot
gw_ops.check.xray_ru_file: The watchdog doesn’t start the gateway xray: its config file sends Russia directly for users without the “Russia direct” choice or the ⚠RU confirmation. The collector redraws the config first; if xray still doesn’t come up, run kaskadctl gw apply and look at the error.
gw_ops.check.xray_ru_open: The gateway xray couldn’t be stopped when Russia direct had to be closed: it may still go directly for users without the “Russia direct” choice or the ⚠RU confirmation. Stop the xray process by hand or reboot the server, then run kaskadctl gw apply.
gw_ops.err.gw_off: The gateway is off: kaskadctl gw enable.
gw_ops.err.host_unknown: Couldn’t detect the server’s address: set the client address — kaskadctl gw host <address or name>.
gw_ops.err.host_not_public: Couldn’t detect the server’s public IP: the route gives the private address {ip}. The client address is unchanged — type the public IP in Settings › Gateway.
gw_ops.err.kind_unsupported: The {kind} protocol isn’t supported in this Kaskad version yet.
gw_ops.err.need_nft: The gateway works only with the new forwarding engine (nftables). Move the forwards first: menu “Forwarding engine and migration”.
gw_ops.err.no_access: The device has no protocols — nothing to change.
gw_ops.err.no_option: the {kind} inbound has no {key} setting; available: {keys}
gw_ops.err.no_usable: The device has no working protocols: grant one (gw device grant) and install it.
gw_ops.err.not_granted: The device doesn’t have the {kind} protocol.
gw_ops.err.not_granted_hint: The device doesn’t have the {kind} inbound: kaskadctl gw device grant {id} {kind}
gw_ops.err.not_installed_hint: The {kind} inbound isn’t installed: kaskadctl gw inbound install {kind}
gw_ops.err.not_installed_xray: {title} isn’t installed: {why} The server is left as it was.
gw_ops.err.not_usable: The {kind} protocol isn’t installed or is off.
gw_ops.err.on_off: the value must be on or off, not {value}
gw_ops.err.pki_kinds: the certificate authority can be changed for the inbound: {kinds}
gw_ops.err.pki_unsupported: The {kind} protocol can’t change its certificate authority in this version.
gw_ops.err.issue_host: Settings for another address go only into a subscription line: files and QR codes use the client address.
gw_ops.err.port_busy: Port {port}/{protos} is in use: {why}. To take it anyway — use --force.
gw_ops.err.teardown_nft: nft didn’t remove the gateway part from the table: {err}
gw_ops.err.vless_443_site: Port 443/tcp is held by the server’s site: VLESS can take 443 only in TLS mode in front of the site, and that’s not possible now — {why}.
gw_ops.err.vless_not_installed: The VLESS protocol isn’t installed: kaskadctl gw inbound install vless (menu 17 → “Protocols”).
gw_ops.err.vless_tls_port: VLESS in TLS mode with its own domain sits on 443 in front of the server’s site: it can’t take another port. Another port is for Reality, and Reality is used when the site on the domain is off.
gw_ops.exit.add_timeout: Adding the key took longer than {minutes} minutes. Reload the “Exits” page: the key may have been added.
gw_ops.exit.all_dup: All these keys are already in the pool.
gw_ops.exit.all_in_pool: All keys are already in the pool.
gw_ops.exit.del_rebuild_failed: Key deleted from the pool, but the rebuild failed: {why}
gw_ops.exit.dup_key: This key is already in the pool.
gw_ops.exit.dup_peer_at: Not adding it twice: {why}. Only one connection with this key will work.
gw_ops.exit.full: The pool already holds the maximum number of keys.
gw_ops.exit.full_hint: Delete a key you don’t need and add again.
gw_ops.exit.gone: This exit is already gone — reload the page.
gw_ops.exit.line_break: Key not added: its text has an invisible line break (usually in the name after #). Copy the key again or erase the name after #.
gw_ops.exit.pool_busy: The key pool is being changed in another window (web panel or menu) — try again in a minute.
gw_ops.exit.pool_changed: The pool has changed — reload the page.
gw_ops.exit.twin_ask: This key is in the pool once more — “{name}”: the routes will move to it.
gw_ops.exit.twin_broken: The routes did not move: {error} — the key is not deleted. A retry will not help: check the gateway first — kaskadctl gw check.
gw_ops.exit.twin_done: The routes moved to “{name}” — the same key.
gw_ops.exit.twin_failed: The routes did not move — the key is not deleted, try again.
gw_ops.exit.twin_unfit: The routes did not move: “{name}” (the same key) is off for the gateway or cannot work — the key is not deleted. Move the routes to another exit and delete it again.
gw_ops.exit.twin_unfit_ask: This key is in the pool once more — “{name}”, but it is off for the gateway or cannot work: the routes will not move to it, and the key will not be deleted. Move the routes to another exit first.
gw_ops.gone.device: The device is already gone — it was deleted earlier.
gw_ops.gone.user: This user is already gone — deleted earlier.
gw_ops.key.empty: Paste a VPN key (vless, hy2, ss, trojan, vmess, vpn://) or the whole text of an AmneziaWG .conf file.
gw_ops.key.not_text: This isn’t a text key file.
gw_ops.key.path: This is a file path, not a key.
gw_ops.key.too_long: The key is longer than {kb} KB — it isn’t an exit key.
gw_ops.log.device_reset_also: GW device reset: {name} ({id}) — {kinds}; the shared password also for: {also}
gw_ops.log.enable: GW enable: gateway on, network {base}, client address {host}
gw_ops.log.inbound_uninstall: GW inbound uninstall: {kind} (port and server keys kept for a reinstall)
gw_ops.log.install_xray_refused: GW inbound install: {kind} not installed — the gateway xray rejected the config
gw_ops.log.issue_mark: GW issue: the “waiting for new settings” mark wasn’t cleared ({err})
gw_ops.log.legs_broken: GW legs: still broken after the repair: {legs}
gw_ops.log.mtu_client: GW MTU: {kind} — client MTU {was} → {now} (network interface MTU too low)
gw_ops.log.mtu_s4: GW MTU: {kind} — new parameters, S4 {was} → {s4} (the server MTU was below 1232); waiting for settings: {n}
gw_ops.log.pki_rotate: GW pki rotate: {kind} — {done}; devices on the inbound: {n}
gw_ops.log.purge: GW purge: gateway removed, inbounds: {inbounds}, services: {units}{people}
gw_ops.log.renumbered: GW exits: pool lines {lines} changed their exit — client connections through them were reset ({n})
gw_ops.log.renumbered_no_conntrack: GW exits: pool lines {lines} changed their exit — conntrack isn’t installed, old client connections weren’t reset (they will reconnect by themselves)
gw_ops.log.restored: GW repair: the gateway part was missing — client connections of {base} were reset ({n})
gw_ops.log.restored_no_conntrack: GW repair: the gateway part was missing — conntrack isn’t installed, old client connections weren’t reset (gw_fwd cuts them; kaskadctl gw enable installs the conntrack package)
gw_ops.log.vless_rekey: GW vless rekey: {done}; devices on the inbound: {n}
gw_ops.mtu.fits: {title}: the server’s network interface MTU fits clients with MTU {mtu} — nothing to change.
gw_ops.mtu.kinds: MTU is set for the WireGuard and AmneziaWG protocols ({kinds}), not for {kind}.
gw_ops.mtu.no_devices: {title}: client MTU {was} → {now}. No devices on this protocol.
gw_ops.mtu.reissue: {title}: client MTU {was} → {now}. Settings issued earlier work, but with the old MTU — reissue them (menu 17 → 2 → 1 or panel → “Users & devices”): {who}.
gw_ops.mtu.s4_done: {title}: S4 {was} → {s4}, server MTU {server}. Settings of this protocol issued earlier won’t connect anymore — reissue them (menu 17 → 2 → 1 or panel → “Users & devices”): {who}.
gw_ops.mtu.s4_done_none: {title}: S4 {was} → {s4}, server MTU {server}. No devices on this protocol.
gw_ops.mtu.s4_no_help: a new S4 won’t help: the server’s network interface MTU is too low
gw_ops.mtu.s4_nobody: to nobody: there are no devices on this protocol
gw_ops.mtu.s4_offer: {title}: new parameters with S4 ≤ {limit} instead of {was}. The protocol will restart and settings issued earlier will stop connecting — reissue them {whom}.
gw_ops.mtu.s4_only: S4 can be changed only for the AmneziaWG 2.0 protocol (awg2).
gw_ops.mtu.s4_whom: to every device of this protocol: {who}
gw_ops.no_exits: Devices have no internet: no exit is working, and on exit failure is set to “block”. Add a working exit key or change the default route.
gw_ops.note.old_port_busy: the previous port {port}/{protos} is in use ({why}) — took {alt}
gw_ops.option.l2tp_plain: L2TP without encryption (for routers without IPsec)
gw_ops.plan.not_in_version: not available in this Kaskad version
gw_ops.port.by_inbound_off: the gateway protocol {title} keeps it (switched off now)
gw_ops.port.by_service: it is a service port of Kaskad: {what}
gw_ops.port.svc.egress: the proxy for the Telegram API
gw_ops.port.effect.foreign_dnat: the gateway protocol would override it
gw_ops.port.effect.ssh: a protocol on this port would cut off SSH access to the server
gw_ops.purge.disable_failed: the gateway didn’t turn off the usual way ({err}) — removing it piece by piece
gw_ops.purge.no_adapter: the {kind} protocol is in the settings, but this version has no adapter for it — its files weren’t removed
gw_ops.purge.table_left: a gateway part is left in the nftables table: {err}
gw_ops.reissue.server_changed: {title}: the server settings changed ({changed}) — settings issued earlier won’t connect. Reissue them (menu 17 → 2 → 1 or panel → “Users & devices”): {who}.
gw_ops.reissue.vless: {what} — VLESS links issued earlier won’t connect. Reissue them (menu 17 → 2 → 1 or panel → “Users & devices”): {who}.
gw_ops.script_fail.awg_core: Couldn’t prepare the AmneziaWG core (amneziawg-go + awg). The repository is private: without a GitHub key it returns 404. What to do (any of): 1) a GitHub key — menu 8 → 6 (or the GH_TOKEN variable when starting gokaskad); 2) a kaskad-pro clone with bin/ in /opt/kaskad-pro; 3) put the files in place by hand: {go} and {tool}.
gw_ops.script_fail.awg_only: The pool has AmneziaWG keys only, and the AmneziaWG core didn’t load.
gw_ops.script_fail.bad_line: The new pool has a line that isn’t a key — the pool is untouched.
gw_ops.script_fail.handover: The routes did not move — the key is not deleted, try again.
gw_ops.script_fail.handover_broken: The routes did not move: the core of the gateway did not answer — the key is not deleted. A retry will not help: check the gateway first — kaskadctl gw check.
gw_ops.script_fail.handover_unfit: The routes did not move: the other copy of the key is off for the gateway or cannot work — the key is not deleted. Move the routes to another exit and delete it again.
gw_ops.script_fail.no_xray: No xray of the pinned version (it didn’t download, or there’s no build for this machine) — the key pool wasn’t rebuilt. Kaskad doesn’t take another xray from the server.
gw_ops.script_fail.parse: Couldn’t parse the keys (no usable VPN key: vless, hy2, ss, trojan, vmess, vpn://, .conf).
gw_ops.script_fail.path: This is a file path, not a key.
gw_ops.script_fail.pool_busy: The key pool is being changed in another window (web panel or menu) — try again in a minute.
gw_ops.script_fail.pool_changed: The pool has changed — try again.
gw_ops.script_fail.rolled_back: Key not added — the pool is left as it was.
gw_ops.script_fail.rolled_back_add: Key not added — the pool is left as it was.
gw_ops.script_fail.rolled_back_replace: Pool not replaced — left as it was.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped: No key added: xray won’t accept them.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.bad_addr: No key added: the client address in the AmneziaWG key is outside private networks or taken by a network of this server — the key won’t do, ask for a new one.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.bad_link: No key added: the keys couldn’t be read (no server address or port, no password, or something not supported).
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.bad_pin: No key added: their certificate fingerprint (pcs) isn’t a SHA-256.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.dup_endpoint: No key added: another Hysteria2 key already uses this server address and port — xray would use the settings of the first one. Remove the old key if you need the new one.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.gw_net: No key added: the client address in the AmneziaWG key falls within the gateway network of this server {net} — move the gateway of one of the servers to another network (in the panel: Settings › Gateway › Gateway network); the devices of the gateway you move will need new keys.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.insecure: No key added: their certificate check is off (allowInsecure) and they have no certificate fingerprint (pcs) — xray no longer accepts such keys. Ask whoever issued them for links with pcs.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.no_tls: No key added: they have no TLS and the server is at a public address (the password would travel in clear text).
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.self_ep: No key added: the server address in the key points to this server — the key won’t do, ask for a new one.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.unsupported_s: No key added: Kaskad doesn’t take such protocols (it needs vless, hy2, ss, trojan, vmess, vpn:// or a .conf).
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.weak_cipher: No key added: they have no encryption or a weak cipher (Shadowsocks none/plain, VMess none/zero).
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.xray_refused: No key added: this version of xray doesn’t accept them — the links have parameters it doesn’t understand or considers wrong. Ask whoever issued the keys for new links.
gw_ops.script_fail.skipped.xray_unchecke: No key added: xray didn’t answer in time, the keys weren’t checked. Try again a bit later.
gw_ops.script_fail.sub_cert: The subscription server’s certificate doesn’t match the address (a subscription by IP with a certificate for a domain?) — add the subscription by domain or over http, or paste its contents.
gw_ops.script_fail.sub_clash: This is a Clash (mihomo) profile — Kaskad can’t read it: you need a subscription with VPN keys (vless, hy2, ss, trojan, vmess, vpn://; in goAmnezia — the “all.vpn” address).
gw_ops.script_fail.sub_fetch: Couldn’t download the subscription — paste its contents.
gw_ops.script_fail.sub_http: The subscription server returned an error (wrong address or the subscription was revoked) — check the address.
gw_ops.script_fail.tmp: Couldn’t create a temporary pool file.
gw_ops.script_fail.xray_field: xray rejected the config: wrong field {field}.
gw_ops.script_fail.xray_field_reality: xray rejected the config: wrong field {field} — check publicKey (pbk) and shortId (sid) in the key: the VLESS server issues them.
gw_ops.script_fail.xray_insecure: xray rejected the config: it no longer accepts keys without a certificate check (allowInsecure) — the key needs the fingerprint of the server certificate (pcs).
gw_ops.script_fail.xray_none: xray rejected the config: xray gave no reason.
gw_ops.script_fail.xray_removed: xray rejected the config: this version of xray no longer supports the setting {feature}.
gw_ops.script_warn.awg_core_missing: AmneziaWG core unavailable — bringing up VLESS keys only (AmneziaWG skipped).
gw_ops.script_warn.ru_held: The gateway has not applied the changes of the domestic exits yet, so their tunnels stay closed for now — no traffic goes the wrong way. The gateway usually applies them on its own within a minute. If the domestic exits in the “Exits” section are still not working a few minutes later, check their state there and repeat your last change of a domestic exit — adding, editing or removing it.
gw_ops.script_warn.awg_key.loss226: Key #{n}: AmneziaWG 3.1 with RandomTrailers, different S1–S4 and H ranges loses ≈7 % of packets (issue #226, same with the kernel module and in userspace). Key accepted; a key with equal S1–S4 or single H values is better.
gw_ops.script_warn.awg_key.lost3x: Key #{n}: AmneziaWG 3.x key added by an old Kaskad version without the 3.x fields — it won’t connect. Delete it and add it again.
gw_ops.script_warn.awg_key.need31: Key #{n}: AmneziaWG 3.1 won’t connect — it needs the 3.1 core. GitHub key: menu 8 → 6, then open this screen again.
gw_ops.script_warn.others: Other pool keys with warnings: {n} — see the list of exits.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.bad_addr: Keys skipped: {n} — the client address in the AmneziaWG key is outside private networks or taken by a network of this server; such keys won’t do, ask for new ones.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.bad_link: Keys skipped: {n} — the keys couldn’t be read.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.bad_pin: Keys skipped: {n} — their certificate fingerprint (pcs) isn’t a SHA-256.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.dup_endpoint: Keys skipped: {n} — a second Hysteria2 key at the same server address and port.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.gw_net: Keys skipped: {n} — the client address in the AmneziaWG key falls within the gateway network of this server {net}; move the gateway of one of the servers to another network (in the panel: Settings › Gateway › Gateway network); the devices of the gateway you move will need new keys.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.insecure: Keys skipped: {n} — their certificate check is off (allowInsecure) and they have no certificate fingerprint (pcs): xray no longer accepts such keys.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.no_tls: Keys skipped: {n} — no TLS to a public address.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.self_ep: Keys skipped: {n} — the server address in the key points to this server; such keys won’t do, ask for new ones.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.unsupported_s: Keys skipped: {n} — Kaskad doesn’t take such protocols.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.weak_cipher: Keys skipped: {n} — no encryption or a weak cipher.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.xray_refused: Keys skipped: {n} — this version of xray doesn’t accept them.
gw_ops.script_warn.skipped.xray_unchecke: Keys skipped: {n} — xray didn’t answer in time, the keys weren’t checked; try again a bit later.
gw_ops.script_warn.tg_group_empty: The bot’s proxy group has no usable keys — the Telegram API proxy is off, the bot goes direct. Move a key into the group or choose another group.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.bad_addr: Key #{n}: the client address in the AmneziaWG key is outside private networks or taken by a network of this server — the exit doesn’t work. The key won’t do, ask for a new one.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.bad_link: Key #{n}: the key couldn’t be read — the exit doesn’t work. Remove it and add the key again.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.bad_pin: Key #{n}: the certificate fingerprint (pcs) isn’t a SHA-256. Remove it and add the link again.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.dup_endpoin: Key #{n}: a second Hysteria2 key at the same server address and port — remove the extra one.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.gw_net: Key #{n}: the client address {addr} falls within the gateway network of this server {net} — the exit doesn’t work. Move the gateway of one of the servers to another network (in the panel: Settings › Gateway › Gateway network); the devices of the gateway you move will need new keys.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.insecure: Key #{n}: VLESS without a certificate check (allowInsecure) — the certificate fingerprint couldn’t be taken, the exit doesn’t work. Update the key or the subscription: it needs a link with the pcs fingerprint.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.no_tls: Key #{n}: no TLS to a public address — the exit doesn’t work. A key with TLS is needed.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.self_ep: Key #{n}: the server address in the key points to this server — the exit doesn’t work. The key won’t do, ask for a new one.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.tofu_wait: Key #{n}: VLESS without a certificate check (allowInsecure) — the server didn’t answer during the update, the exit doesn’t work yet. Kaskad will try again by itself, at most once an hour (for up to 7 days).
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.unsupported: Key #{n}: Kaskad doesn’t take this protocol — the exit doesn’t work.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.weak_cipher: Key #{n}: no encryption or a weak cipher — the exit doesn’t work.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.xray_ext: Key #{n}: added before xray was installed; xray has now checked it — the key works with all its parameters (fm, extra, ech, pqv or VLESS encryption).
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.xray_legacy: Key #{n}: xray didn’t accept its new parameters (fm, extra, ech, pqv or VLESS encryption) — the key is built without them, as in 3.3.5.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.xray_refuse: Key #{n}: this version of xray doesn’t accept it, with its new parameters or without them — the exit is off, the other keys work. The same link won’t help — ask whoever issued the key for a new link.
gw_ops.script_warn.vless_key.xray_unchec: Key #{n}: xray didn’t answer in time, the key wasn’t checked — try again a bit later.
gw_ops.script_warn.xray_builtin: Couldn’t download a separate xray — using the built-in one.
gw_ops.support.nft_refused: nft rejected the gateway table (no TPROXY in the kernel?): {err}
gw_ops.unit.dns_direct: gateway DNS for the devices going directly
gw_ops.vless.block_off: the VLESS protocol or the gateway is off
gw_ops.vless.block_reality: VLESS stayed on Reality next to the site (port {port}): kaskadctl gw vless sync will try to switch to TLS
gw_ops.vless.site_on: a regular site is on at {domain}; VLESS is on 443 with its own certificate, the panel is also at https://{domain}/…
gw_ops.vless.site_not_on: the site on {domain} is not on: {why}. VLESS works on the backup Reality; once the cause is gone — “Retry TLS” (kaskadctl gw vless mode tls)
gw_ops.vless.cert_auto_tls: The site on {domain} was switched on by itself: VLESS went on TLS with its own certificate (no devices with VLESS — nobody to give keys out again).
gw_ops.log.vless_site_not_on: VLESS: the site was not switched on at the install ({why}) — VLESS on Reality
gw_ops.log.vless_cert_busy: VLESS: the switch to TLS after the certificate was skipped — a change of the mode is running

gw_ops.vless.cert_busy: The switch of VLESS to TLS is put off: a change of the mode is running — repeat “Switch on TLS” later (kaskadctl gw vless mode tls).
gw_ops.warn.base_overlaps: the gateway network {base} overlaps with the server’s own networks ({why}); to change it — in the panel: Settings › Gateway › Gateway network
gw_ops.warn.gates: ExecStartPre of the inbounds not written: {err}
gw_ops.warn.host_private: the server’s public address wasn’t detected ({address} is private): set the client address — kaskadctl gw host <address or name>
gw_ops.warn.legs_down: AmneziaWG exits aren’t working yet: {n} of the pool. If there’s no AmneziaWG core, set a GitHub key (menu 8 → 6); details — menu 17 → “Status”
gw_ops.warn.no_adapter: the {kind} protocol is in the settings, but this version has no adapter for it
gw_ops.warn.no_conntrack: conntrack isn’t installed ({err}): after the table is lost, the watchdog won’t reset old client connections — gw_fwd cuts them
gw_ops.warn.no_xray: {err} SOCKS5, the VLESS protocol and VLESS exits don’t work until xray is there.
gw_ops.warn.pool_unread: the exit pool couldn’t be read ({err}) — xray and DNS are left as they were, clients stay on the exits of the last check
gw_ops.warn.rebased: device addresses changed — reissue their settings
gw_ops.warn.xray_deferred: Settings saved, xray applies them within 20 s
gw_ops.warn.xray_down: {err} The gateway xray isn’t running: SOCKS5, the VLESS protocol and VLESS exits don’t work.
gw_ops.warn.xray_ru_closed: {err} The previous config sent Russia directly for users who no longer get it under the new settings, so the gateway xray is stopped: SOCKS5, the VLESS protocol and VLESS exits don’t work until xray takes the new config (fix the cause and run kaskadctl gw apply).
gw_ops.warn.xray_ru_open: {err} The previous config may still send Russia directly for users who no longer get it under the new settings: Kaskad tried disable, stop and kill, but the gateway xray didn’t stop. Stop the xray process by hand or reboot the server, then run kaskadctl gw apply.
gw_ops.err.hy2_hop_port: Port {port}/udp is inside the port hopping range {hop} — pick a port outside the range.
gw_ops.err.hy2_hop_busy: The range {hop} does not fit — taken: {busy}.
gw_ops.err.hy2_cert: The Hysteria2 certificate: domain or self, got {value}.
gw_ops.hy2.reissue: The Hysteria2 links given out stop working — issue them again: {who}.
gw_ops.note.hy2_hop_dropped: Port hopping {hop} is not brought back: {why}. Turn it on again with another range.
gw_ops.exit.role_id_changed: The key of exit {id} was not moved: its id would change after the move — the key stays where it was.
gw_ops.err.key_in_other_role: This key is already among the {where} exits ({id}) — move it to the group you need instead of adding it again.
gw_ops.exit.ru_added: The key was added to the domestic exits.
gw_ops.exit.ru_added_n: Keys added to the domestic exits: {n}.
gw_ops.exit.ru_full: There can be no more than {max} domestic keys.
gw_ops.exit.ru_none: No new keys: these keys are there already.
gw_ops.exit.ru_no_sub: Add a subscription link under “Subscriptions” with its group — its keys then stay in that group.
gw_ops.exit.role_move_failed: The key of exit {id} was not moved: {err} The key stays where it was — try the move again.
gw_ops.exit.role_move_stuck: The move of the key of exit {id} broke off and could not be undone: the key is now {where}. Try the move again.
gw_ops.exit.role_move_half: The key of exit {id} was moved, but the exit did not get into the group ({err}), and the key could not be put back ({back}). Try the move again.
gw_ops.where.both: among both the foreign and the domestic exits
gw_ops.err.keys_in_other_role: Keys already among the domestic exits: {n} — not added. Move the exit you need to the group instead of adding it again.
gw_ops.err.vless_443_mode: Port 443/tcp is held by the server’s site: VLESS takes 443 only in TLS mode in front of the site. Changing the port doesn’t change the mode — switch to TLS: kaskadctl gw vless mode tls (the VLESS links will have to be given out again).
gw_ops.err.vless_443_mode_not: Port 443/tcp is held by the server’s site: VLESS takes 443 only in TLS mode in front of the site (kaskadctl gw vless mode tls), and that’s not possible now — {why}.
gw_ops.settings.no_net: The protocol network comes in a later release.
gw_ops.settings.no_tls: {title}: TLS versions are not set here.
gw_ops.settings.tls_bad: {title}: these TLS versions do not fit. Possible: {choices}.
gw_ops.settings.tls_hint.only12: if the hoster or the network breaks TLS 1.3
gw_ops.settings.tls_note.vless: VLESS connections use TLS 1.3 anyway; “1.3 only” closes TLS 1.2 for the site behind VLESS.
gw_ops.settings.tls_warn.sstp: Windows 10 and MikroTik may fail to connect: they have no TLS 1.3 by default.
gw_ops.settings.tls_warn.sstp_who: SSTP devices on Windows and MikroTik: {who}.
gw_ops.settings.tls_warn.ocserv: Old OpenConnect applications may fail to connect.
gw_ops.settings.proto_alone: The protocol, udp or tcp, goes together with the port.
gw_ops.settings.nothing: {title}: nothing to change — these settings are already in place.
gw_ops.settings.via_xray: If you opened the panel through VLESS, SOCKS5 or Hysteria2 of this server, the connection may drop.
gw_ops.settings.reissue_hard: Devices with the previous {title} settings won’t connect — issue their settings again: {who}.
gw_ops.settings.reissue_soft: It’s better to issue the {title} settings again: {who}.
gw_ops.settings.undo_nothing: {title}: there are no previous settings to return.
gw_ops.settings.undo_need_yes: {title}: returning the previous settings ({what}) needs a confirmation. {lines}
gw_ops.settings.undo_hit: You are connected through {what}: the link may drop after the restore, and a restore has no rollback in 2 min.
gw_ops.settings.undo_changed: {title}: the settings were changed once more — nothing to return.
gw_ops.settings.undo_port_busy: {title}: the previous port {port} is now in use: {why}. Choose another port.
gw_ops.settings.pending_note: Confirm in the panel or with kaskadctl gw pending confirm within 2 min — otherwise the settings come back.
gw_ops.settings.restart.syncconf: {what}: no restart — the new port is taken on the fly.
gw_ops.settings.restart.live: {what}: changes on the fly, no restart.
gw_ops.settings.restart.awg: {what}: restart for 15–25 s; devices with the old settings won’t connect until they get the new ones.
gw_ops.settings.restart.ovpn: {what}: the OpenVPN instance whose port changed restarts; devices with the old settings won’t connect to it until they get the new ones.
gw_ops.settings.restart.ocserv: {what}: the OpenConnect service restarts — all its connections drop.
gw_ops.settings.restart.sstp: {what}: accel-ppp restarts — L2TP and PPTP connections drop for a few seconds too.
gw_ops.settings.restart.xray: {what}: the gateway xray restarts for a few seconds — exits through xray and the gateway DNS drop for that time too.
gw_ops.settings.sessions_cut: {n} connection (SSTP, L2TP, PPTP) will drop.|{n} connections (SSTP, L2TP, PPTP) will drop.
gw_ops.settings.front_no_safe: {title}: on 443 next to the site VLESS moves by a switch of its mode — a safe apply with a rollback isn’t available here. Apply without it or pick another port.
gw_ops.settings.front_note: Port 443 is the site’s: VLESS will stand in front of the site and move to TLS with its own domain — the links of every device change. The previous settings can’t be returned after this switch.
gw_ops.settings.last_failed: The record of the last application wasn’t written ({err}) — the previous settings can’t be returned after this application.
gw_ops.settings.after_failed: {title}: the settings are applied, but the last step failed ({err}): whom to give the settings again may be unmarked. Check the devices or return the previous settings.
gw_ops.settings.after_failed_no_undo: {title}: the settings are applied, but the last step failed ({err}): whom to give the settings again may be unmarked. Check the devices.
gw_ops.log.after_failed: GW: a step after the write failed ({err}) — the write is made, the wait and the record of the last application are kept
gw_ops.settings.undo_moved: {title}: the protocol’s settings were changed by another action since (now {now}) — the previous ones can’t be brought back.
gw_ops.settings.undo_front: {title}: the previous port 443 is the site’s — VLESS can go back to it only by a switch of its mode.
gw_ops.log.reissue_mark: GW: the mark «waiting for new settings» wasn’t written ({err})
gw_ops.log.preview_note: GW: the note of new settings downloaded (issue-preview.json) failed ({err}) — the mark «waiting for new settings» stays
gw_ops.log.last_failed: GW: the record of a protocol’s last application wasn’t written ({err})
gw_ops.log.xray_after_failed: GW: xray wasn’t restarted after the panel’s answer ({err}) — the collector will retry by itself (usually within a minute); a refusal of xray goes to the event feed
gw_ops.settings.no_undo: {title}: a safe apply isn’t available — the previous settings aren’t recorded ({err}). It can’t be applied with a rollback.
gw_ops.settings.last_refused: {title}: the record of the last application couldn’t be written ({err}) — without it there’s neither a return to the previous settings nor a rollback. Nothing was applied.
